slides.title: Feedback and Closed-Loop Control

slides.title: Second Order Linear System

visualInspection.notes: Mass–spring–damper diagram has positive x to the right and restoring/viscous forces −kx and −bẋ. The homogeneous equation is mẍ+bẋ+kx=0. m is mass, b viscous damping coefficient, k stiffness. Weak spring/heavy damping can be sluggish; stiff spring/light damping can oscillate, with formal threshold on following slides. slides.title: Second Order Linear System

visualInspection.notes: Positive-parameter damping classification: discriminant positive gives real unequal overdamped poles; negative gives complex underdamped poles; zero gives critical damping. slides.title: Second Order Linear System

visualInspection.notes: Distinct real-root solution is c₁e^(s₁t)+c₂e^(s₂t), constants from initial position and velocity. Plot shows two negative real poles, s₁ farther left than s₂. slides.title: Second Order Linear System

visualInspection.notes: Conjugate roots λ±iμ are expanded using Euler’s identity into e^(λt)[C₁cos(μt)+C₂sin(μt)]. Real motion requires the appropriate conjugate coefficients; C₁=c₁+c₂ and C₂=i(c₁−c₂). The final real constants can be written r cosδ and r sinδ. slides.title: Second Order Linear System

visualInspection.notes: Amplitude-phase form is r e^(λt) cos(μt−δ), with r from the real cosine/sine coefficients and δ=atan2(sine coefficient,cosine coefficient). slides.title: Second Order Linear System

visualInspection.notes: Normalized polynomial s²+2ζω_n s+ω_n²=0. ζ=b/(2√km), ω_n=√(k/m), λ=−ζω_n, and μ=ω_n√(1−ζ²) for the underdamped case. No damping has b=ζ=0; positive critical damping has ζ=1. Natural frequency is not damped oscillation frequency. slides.title: Control of Second Order Linear Systems

visualInspection.notes: Critical direct-feedback design uses b′=2√(mk′). Gains themselves may be negative while total effective damping/stiffness stay positive. slides.title: Control Law Partitioning

visualInspection.notes: Partitioned force f=αf′+β uses α=m and β=bẋ+kx. Exact matching cancels damping/stiffness, yielding ẍ=f′, a normalized acceleration input. slides.title: Disturbance Rejection

visualInspection.notes: BIBO means bounded disturbance magnitude implies bounded error for a stable closed-loop transfer function. slides.title: Disturbance Rejection

visualInspection.notes: For constant normalized error forcing d and stable positive k_p,k_v, steady-state derivatives vanish and e_ss=d/k_p. Larger positive k_p reduces magnitude for a fixed nonzero d. Error is never zero requires nonzero disturbance and finite gain; it is not true for zero forcing. slides.title: Disturbance Rejection

visualInspection.notes: Integral action adds k_i∫e dt to servo and error equation. High-resolution rendering confirms the differentiated equation has e triple-dot and f_dist DOT on the right. Constant forcing has zero derivative after its onset. Stable steady state with k_i≠0 can yield e=0. The characteristic polynomial is s³+k_v s²+k_p s+k_i; positive gains alone do not guarantee stability. Initial integrator state and onset discontinuities must not be erased by differentiation.
